messages:
Mia (Product Designer): put a quick mock in the figma for the model catalog compare view — link: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz (please comment). Main asks: re-order filters, accessibility for performance badges, and version-pinning affordance. Thoughts? :eyes:
Raj (Frontend): looked — love the compact cards. Quick take: filter order should match how people make decisions. I think latency first, then cost, then accuracy.
Leah (Research): for our 40 interviews most PMs sorted by latency or cost depending on production need. Suggest primary filters = {latency, cost, region}, secondary = {accuracy, model-size, quantization}.
Ava (Design PM): agree with Leah. Also we should avoid deep nested popovers for pinning — users get lost. Maybe inline pin toggle on the card header?
Connor (Infra): backend can support compound filters and sorting. One caveat: perf badges currently computed async; if we render them for 50 cards it spikes telemetry. We should lazy-load badges or show placeholders.
Mia (Product Designer): good call Connor — propose placeholder skeleton + aria-label saying "performance metrics loading" for screen readers. Also badges need alt text and color-contrast. Current amber badge (AA: 2.8) fails WCAG.
Raj (Frontend): will add aria-labels. For colors, can we switch to darker tones or add an icon+label so color isn't the only cue?
Leah (Research): icon + concise text (e.g., ⚡ Low latency) helped in tests. Also add a tooltip with metric breakouts on hover/focus.
Ava (Design PM): for compare table UX — do we keep the current wide table or switch to stacked responsive cards for narrow screens?
Mia (Product Designer): I'd like responsive cards for mobile, table for desktop. But ensure keyboard nav across the table cells (tab/arrow keys).
Connor (Infra): arrow-key nav is fine client-side, but we need to ensure virtualization doesn't drop focus on scroll. Frontend should preserve DOM nodes for focused rows.
Raj (Frontend): noted — will implement focus preservation and add role="table" semantics + aria-describedby for the header.
Mia (Product Designer): version pinning: current mock shows a pin icon that opens a small menu to select version. Concerns: discoverability and accidental pins. Proposed pattern: long-press/hover reveals version list, clicking pin opens confirm inline with "pin for this route" checkbox.
Leah (Research): in test users mis-clicked the tiny pin. Make the target >= 44px and add a confirmation toast + undo (5s).
Ava (Design PM): undo toast sounds good. No modal needed. Also we should show pinned state in the model card and on the route config page (sync).
Raj (Frontend): small technical note: pinning should be idempotent and we have an API endpoint for /routes/:id/pin -> returns 200 with new pin metadata. We'll add optimistic UI and rollback on error.
Connor (Infra): watch for rollout race conditions if two users pin different versions simultaneously. We should surface conflicts in console logs and include etags on the route resource.
Mia (Product Designer): accessibility nits: ensure badges readable by screen readers ("Latency: 18ms, Accuracy: 92%"), table headers announce sort order, and filters are reachable via keyboard and screen-reader friendly labels.
Raj (Frontend): will add sr-only text for badges and use aria-live for sort updates.
design-bot: screenshot-updated: https://cdn.redwood.ai/design/snap-1742005123-1.png (automated render)
Leah (Research): one more thing — add a 'Recently used' filter bucket at top for teams that rerun same models. We saw high value in that pattern.
Mia (Product Designer): good idea — I'll update the figma to include Recently used at the very left of the filter bar and increase pin hit area. Will also change badge color + add icons.
Ava (Design PM): let's aim to ship the table/a11y fixes in next sprint. I'll create tickets and prioritize: 1) badge a11y + lazy-load, 2) filter grouping + UI, 3) pin affordance + undo, 4) keyboard nav.
Raj (Frontend): assigning myself for 1 & 4.
Connor (Infra): I'll handle API etag and conflict handling for pin endpoints.
Leah (Research): I'll draft microcopy for badges/tooltips and run a small follow-up test next week.
Mia (Product Designer): thanks all — will post updated figma and a small demo GIF. If no objections I'll push the changes by EOD and add the tickets. :sparkles:
Ava (Design PM): no objections from me. Scheduling 30m sync tomorrow @10am to finalize microcopy. :calendar:
